explanation: Laundry-and-grooming detector: the pole fires on text about washing, bleaching, ironing, drying, dyeing, trimming or de-staining garments, towels, fabric, leather, hair or fur, and on the garment/hair nouns themselves; in such a passage it is active across much of the sentence with peaks of 4-16 on its mid-clause words ('wash the shirt to remove any stains' 16.2, 'the dress/hair should be trimmed and blended' 14.7/13.3, 'press the seams flat with a warm iron' 9.9, 'coloured shirts and towels' 5.7, 'a mild detergent for delicate fabrics' 6.8, 'her hair was long and dark' 8.3), while the same verbs and syntax about plans, budgets, reports, meetings, metal, wood or beans stay at 0.1-2.3 ('the plan should be trimmed and blended' 0.5, 'press the metal flat' 0.4, 'the budget was approved' 0.1, 'he shaved the wood' 2.2), with cleaning instructions aimed at other surfaces landing in between (car 9.0, floor 6.1, engine 7.2). A separate token-level component that this claim does not cover fires on frequent word-initial fragments of non-Latin scripts (Greek ' κ' 6-11, Cyrillic ' к' 3-12, Persian ' ک', German ' gek' 12.3) and on rare word-initial subwords (' mant', ' unc', 'it', 'acet'); English garment nouns fire even out of domain ('hairline crack' 6.7, 'coat of paint' 4.6) and are the main leftovers.
